question: Does a prospectively fixed joint first-party MTF plus density-aligned 48-micrometre diffuse-RMS signature robustly separate current Velvia 50 from every retained VISION3 observed source profile, especially the MTF-near 50D profile?

comparison.density_alignment: For each Kodak layer, subtract its minimum traced characteristic density, solve the monotone piecewise-linear curve at 1.0 D above that minimum, and evaluate the same layer's log-linear diffuse-RMS curve at the recovered log-relative exposure.
comparison.kodak_granularity_composite: geometric mean of the three density-aligned layer Sigma-D values
comparison.velvia_granularity_compatibility_hypothe: Interpret the reported Fujifilm RMS granularity value 9 as 0.009 D at the stated 1.0 D above minimum and 48-micrometre aperture; this is an explicit cross-manufacturer compatibility hypothesis, not a source-stated unit equivalence.
comparison.mtf_distance: reuse the exact current-Velvia-to-Kodak normalized-log-shape RMSE from U5.R2BW0
comparison.joint_distance: Euclidean norm of MTF distance and absolute natural-log granularity ratio

stop_rules: Do not change the 0.001 conversion, density anchor, layer composite, sensitivity interval, metric or thresholds after any score.
Any failed source integrity, inversion, nominal, sensitivity or every-profile gate closes this exact joint signature.

A pass may retain only a non-renderable cross-manufacturer source-domain observation; it cannot identify independent rolls, process/scanner-invariant stock response, NPS, colour appearance, an RGB operator or a product profile.
claim_ceiling: Prospective compatibility test joining exact first-party MTF and 48-micrometre diffuse-RMS observations under an explicit cross-manufacturer unit/alignment hypothesis and E-6/ECN-2 confounds; not calibration, independent replication, photographic appearance, render or product evidence.
